disease_label_per_paper: Severe diabetic foot attack / diabetic foot ulcer infection with deep collection, gas, and chronic osteomyelitis
presentation_summary: 55-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, metastatic renal cell carcinoma on chemotherapy, and immunotherapy-associated hepatitis presented with 24 hours of increasing swelling and redness of the left foot with superficial blistering.
He had injured the plantar left foot on holiday and had a non-healing plantar ulcer for more than a year, managed without surgery.
Presentation exam showed a red, hot, swollen left foot with an infected plantar ulcer; CRP was 295 mg/L and HbA1c was 95 mmol/mol.

MRI showed a 48 x 37 x 35 mm collection from dorsal to plantar foot between the second and third metatarsal heads, chronic osteomyelitis around the third metatarsal head, and gas/extension along the posterior compartment.
He underwent repeated debridement/washout, local antibiotic beads, ICU care for hemodynamic instability/sepsis, and recovered with secondary-intention wound healing.
